title: Will the American Dream still include owning a home?
主要内容: The article explores whether the American Dream still includes owning a home. Despite the housing crisis and mortgage crash, most Americans still desire home ownership. Fannie Mae's survey shows 70% of respondents would buy a home if they were moving, indicating the aspiration remains unchanged. HUD Secretary Shaun Donovan notes that the aspiration for home ownership is consistent, though the rules of funding have changed. Critics argue that the push for home ownership during the housing boom led to over-leveraging, and now underwriting is tighter. President Obama emphasized that hard work and responsibility should be rewarded through home ownership but warned against repeating past mistakes. Home ownership rates have declined from a peak of 69% to 65.2%. The article also discusses a proposed bill to dismantle Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, shifting mortgage finance to private investors. However, private investors remain cautious, limiting their involvement in the mortgage market. The article also highlights the growing single-family rental market, which has expanded from 10 million to 15 million homes, supported by institutional investors. Laurie Hawkes, president of American Residential Properties, argues that rental housing is becoming a preferred option for middle-class families and millennials, who value financial flexibility and job mobility. Fannie Mae's Duncan disputes this, stating that the stigma of renting has diminished, but the aspiration to own a home remains. He notes that younger generations are delaying home ownership due to longer education and career paths. The article also mentions that wealth creation is increasingly urban, with 80% of wealth generated in cities, as noted by MIT researchers. The future of home ownership may involve smaller units, co-ops, and services for seniors, adapting to changing societal needs.
